title: Optimising Graphical Approaches to Multiple Testing Procedures
text: multigrain (Multiple Testing using Graphical Approaches; Improve power Numerical Optimisation) R package finds optimal graphical multiple testing procedure clinical trial. Confirmatory trials routinely test multiple hypotheses — across endpoints, doses, subpopulations — must strongly control family-wise error rate (FWER). Graphical approaches popular framework , choosing hypothesis weights transition matrix make graph typically done hand. multigrain automates : given simulated p-values user-defined trial success measure (function scores possible pattern hypothesis rejections), searches hypothesis weights transition weights find graph maximises expected trial success. result valid graphical test strongly controls FWER.

text: end--end example four hypotheses: two primary (H1, H2) two secondary (H3, H4). Secondaries gated corresponding primaries (H3 can tested H1 rejected; H4 H2).

title: Optimising Graphical Approaches to Multiple Testing Procedures
text: Assume one-sided test statistics jointly normal. Provide per-hypothesis nominal power (unadjusted multiplicity) correlation matrix:
code: library(multigrain)  power_nominal <- c(0.95, 0.90, 0.85, 0.80) corr_mat <- matrix(     c(         1.0, 0.5, 0.4, 0.2,         0.5, 1.0, 0.2, 0.4,         0.4, 0.2, 1.0, 0.5,         0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 1.0     ),     nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE )  set.seed(1) pvals <- simulate_pvalues(     power_nominal = power_nominal,     corr_matrix = corr_mat,     nsim = 1e5 )

title: Optimising Graphical Approaches to Multiple Testing Procedures
text: Use trial_success() express “success” means trial. variables r1, r2, r3, r4 binary indicators — ri = 1 hypothesis Hi rejected, 0 otherwise. can combine arithmetic (+, *) logical (&&, ||) operators.
code: # Average power: mean proportion of hypotheses rejected avg_power <- trial_success(0.25 * (r1 + r2 + r3 + r4))  # Disjunctive power: at least one rejection disjunctive <- trial_success(r1 || r2 || r3 || r4)  # Custom: require a primary rejection, with extra credit for the # gated secondary (H3 adds value only if H1 is also rejected, etc.) custom_success <- trial_success(     0.25 * (2 * (r1 || r2) + r1 * r3 + r2 * r4) )

title: Optimising Graphical Approaches to Multiple Testing Procedures
text: Use graph_constraint() encode structural rules — example, primaries receive initial alpha, secondaries can receive alpha recycled gating primary: NA means “free optimise” fixed number means “held constant”.
code: gc <- graph_constraint(     hyp_constraint  = c(NA, NA, 0, 0),     trans_constraint = matrix(         c(             0, NA, NA, 0,             NA, 0, 0, NA,             0, 1, 0, 0,             1, 0, 0, 0         ),         nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE     ) )

title: Optimising Graphical Approaches to Multiple Testing Procedures
code: g_opt <- graph_optimise(     pvals = pvals,     trial_success = custom_success,     graph_constraint = gc )  summary(g_opt) plot(g_opt)

title: Optimising Graphical Approaches to Multiple Testing Procedures
text: Compute multiplicity-adjusted power custom trial success measures optimised graph:
code: calc_power_pvals(     pvals,     hyp_weight   = g_opt$hyp_weight,     trans_matrix = g_opt$trans_matrix,     custom_power = list(         AvgPower      = avg_power,         Disjunctive   = disjunctive,         CustomSuccess = custom_success   ) )

title: Create a trial success function — trial_success
text: code, \(\psi\) written using symbols r1, r2, ..., rm, ri binary indicator hypothesis \(H_i\) rejected chosen graph. can combine indicators arithmetic (+ - * /) logical operators (&&, ||, words , ) reflect design priorities (e.g., “success”, “successes”, weighted composites). utility \(\psi\) evaluated simulated rejection pattern averaged, yielding expected trial success given graph data-generating scenario. lets optimise graphs utility captures clinical/regulatory goals, rather single power summary.

title: Create a trial success function — trial_success
code: # Expected number of rejections (equals m × average power) exp_rejs <- trial_success(r1 + r2 + r3 + r4) #> ✔ Trial success function compiled and sourced successfully.  # \donttest{ # Disjunctive success: any rejection among four disj_power <- trial_success(r1 || r2 || r3 || r4) #> ✔ Trial success function compiled and sourced successfully.  # Conjunctive success: all four must be rejected conj_power <- trial_success(r1 && r2 && r3 && r4) #> ✔ Trial success function compiled and sourced successfully.  # Composite utility: require H1 AND H2 rejection to get H3 and H4 value composite <- trial_success((r1 && r2) * (r3 + r4)) #> ✔ Trial success function compiled and sourced successfully.  # Weighted priorities (e.g., H1 gets weight 2 times H2 or H3) weighted <- trial_success(2*r1 + r2 + r3) #> ✔ Trial success function compiled and sourced successfully.  # Inject values from your environment with !! w <- 2 trial_success(!!w * r1 + r2 + r3) #> ✔ Trial success function compiled and sourced successfully. #> <multigrain_trial_success> #> 2 * r1 + r2 + r3  # Programmatic string input expr_str <- sprintf("%s * r1 + r2", w) trial_success(!!expr_str) #> ✔ Trial success function compiled and sourced successfully. #> <multigrain_trial_success> #> 2 * r1 + r2  # }

title: multigrain 0.2.0
text: Advanced optimisation configuration now handled via new multigrain_control object family control_*() functions. main optimisation functions (optimise_graph(), optimise_graph_parallel()) take single control argument, providing unified extensible API setting optimisation parameters. Users can set parallelisation options (num_threads, grain_size), multigrain_control() + control_parallel(). Default behaviour use single thread. optimise_graph() optimise_graph_parallel() now use memory efficient implementation Bretz shortcut algorithm internal functions graph_shortcut() graph_shortcut_parallel(). full CTP still available apply_ctp() - used Simes parametric graph optimisation future releases.
